rounds.text: Nava Ltd is significantly undervalued by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of 17.2x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 8.2x that sits well below the sector benchmark of 10.36x [E11]. A discounted cash flow model explicitly points to an intrinsic value of Rs 1197 per share compared to its current market price of Rs 574, establishing a massive margin of safety at 52.1% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price misprices the company by only pricing in 2.9% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 13.0% [E47], completely ignoring recent stellar performance metrics such as a 126% YoY net profit surge [E68] and accelerating results that score 100/100 [E73]. Operational efficiency is exceptional, underscored by a high ROA of 6.76% beating the sector benchmark of 2.02% [E8], robust cash conversion of 2.23x backed by Rs 2,312 Cr in operating cash flow [E34, E35], and improving debtor days dropping from 126 to 80.7 days [E60]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over 3 years is -14% [E20], the 12-month price return sits at -9.1% [E52], and institutional money flow shows a negative reading [E44].

Nava Ltd's medium-term earnings performance reveals fundamental weakness, highlighted by a 3-year compounded profit decline of -14% [E20] and sluggish trailing twelve-month profit growth of 2% [E21], demonstrating that 5-year share price growth of 57% has decoupled from profit growth of 13% [E56]. Profitability remains constrained, with recent Return on Equity coming in at just 9% [E9, E29] and operating margins contracting by 5 percentage points over three years down to 40% [E30]. Balance sheet risk is mounting as total borrowings expanded to Rs 3,005 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 2,226 Cr a year earlier [E39], while accounting flags warn that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E64]. Institutional investors are departing given negative institutional money flow [E44, E70], while technical weakness leaves the stock lagging the broader market with a relative strength rating of 17 [E51, E71], trading below its 200-day moving average [E50, E72] alongside high annualised volatility of 51.0% [E54]. Conceded: recent quarterly momentum showed net profit rising +126% YoY [E68] accompanied by strong cash conversion of 2.23x [E34]. Nevertheless, with 5-year sales growth flagged as poor at 11.0% [E62], a cyclical earnings profile [E58], inconsistent yearly operating margin trends [E32], and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -85.2% [E53], the stock carries persistent operational and downside risks.

The bear points to a 3-year compounded profit decline of -14% [E20] and 2% TTM growth [E21], but ignores that recent quarterly results completely reverse this trend with net profit surging +126% YoY [E68] and sales jumping +30% YoY [E66], backed by an insider-bias checklist emphasizing that results score a maximum 100/100 and should not be dismissed on stale sentiment [E73]. Conceded: operating margins contracted over three years [E30] and 5-year sales growth is flagged as poor [E62], but quarterly operating margins have concurrently rebounded by 5 percentage points [E31], debtor days have dramatically improved from 126 to 80.7 days [E60], and working capital requirements have dropped from 163 to 129 days [E61]. While borrowings increased to Rs 3,005 Cr [E39], this coincides with a massive +49.3% build-up in capital-work-in-progress to Rs 3,263 Cr [E40], representing active growth spend rather than idle debt, perfectly supported by robust operating cash flow of Rs 2,312 Cr [E35] and exceptional cash conversion of 2.23x where profits are fully backed by cash [E34]. Conceded: institutional money flow shows a recent outflow [E44, E70] and the stock trades below its 200-day moving average [E50, E72], yet promoters and foreign/domestic institutions have actually increased their stakes over the broader comparison period, with promoters holding 50.03% [E41], foreign institutions rising to 9.73% [E42], and domestic institutions climbing to 0.47% [E43].

Conceded: recent quarterly net profit surged +126% YoY and sales jumped +30% YoY [E66, E68], but the bull glosses over the severe medium-term earnings decay that produced a 3-year compounded profit decline of -14% [E20] and a meager 2% TTM growth rate [E21]. Conceded: quarterly operating margins rebounded by 5 percentage points [E31], but this comes on the heels of an inconsistent yearly trend [E32] and a multi-year operating margin contraction from 45% down to 40% in the TTM period [E30]. While the bull points to active growth spend in CWIP of Rs 3,263 Cr [E40], it ignores the alarming direct warning from filed statements that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E64] while borrowings simultaneously ballooned to Rs 3,005 Cr [E39]. Conceded: promoters and institutional stakes show multi-year increases [E41, E42, E43], but current metrics explicitly highlight a recent institutional outflow with negative money flow [E44, E70].
